# BAB I

## KETENTUAN UMUM

#### Pasal 1

Dalam Peraturan Daerah ini, yang dimaksud dengan:  
1. Kabupaten adalah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
2. Pemerintah Kabupaten adalah Pemerintah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
3. Bupati adalah Bupati Ogan Komering Ulu.  
4. Perangkat Daerah yang selanjutnya disingkat PD adalah Perangkat Daerah di Lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
5. Gender adalah konsep yang mengacu pada pembedaan peran dan tanggung jawab laki-laki dan perempuan yang terjadi akibat dari dan dapat berubah oleh keadaan sosial dan budaya masyarakat.  
6. Kesetaraan Gender yang selanjutnya disingkat KG adalah kesamaan kondisi bagi laki-laki dan perempuan untuk memperoleh kesempatan dan hak-haknya sebagai manusia, agar mampu berperan dan berpartisipasi dalam kegiatan politik, ekonomi, sosial budaya, pertahanan dan keamanan dan kesamaan dalam menikmati hasil pembangunan.  
7. Analisis Gender adalah proses yang dibangun secara sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi dan memahami pembagian kerja atau peran laki-laki dan perempuan, akses, dan kontrol terhadap sumber-sumber daya pembangunan, partisipasi dalam proses pembangunan dan manfaat yang mereka nikmati.  
8. Pengarusutamaan Gender yang selanjutnya disingkat PUG adalah strategi yang dibangun untuk mengintegrasikan gender menjadi satu dimensi integral -3- dari perencanaan, penyusunan, pelaksanaan, pemantauan, dan evaluasi atas kebijakan, program dan kegiatan pembangunan di daerah.  
9. Responsif gender adalah suatu kebijakan, program, kegiatan, dan penganggaran yang memperkecil perbedaan, kebutuhan, pengalaman, dan aspirasi laki-laki dan perempuan.  
10. Anggaran Responsif Gender selanjutnya disingkat ARG adalah anggaran yang respon terhadap kebutuhan perempuan dan laki-laki yang tujuan untuk mewujudkan kesetaraan dan keadilan gender.  
11. Pemberdayaan perempuan adalah upaya perempuan untuk memperoleh akses dan kontrol terhadap sumber daya, ekonomi, politik, sosial, budaya, agar perempuan dapat mengatur diri dan meningkatkan rasa percaya diri untuk mampu berperan dan berpartisipasi aktif dalammemecahkan masalah, sehingga mampu membangun kemampuan dan konsep diri.  
12. Perlindungan perempuan adalah segala upaya yang ditujukan untuk melindungi perempuan dan memberikan rasaaman dalam pemenuhan hak-haknya dengan memberikan perhatian yang konsisten dan sistematis yang ditujukan untuk mencapai kesetaraan gender.  
13. Anak adalah seseorang yang belum berusia 18 (delapanbelas) tahun, termasuk anak yang masih dalamkandungan.  
14. Perlindungan Anak adalah segala kegiatan untuk menjamindan melindungi Anak dan hak-haknya agar dapat hidup, tumbuh, berkembang, dan berpartisipasi secara optimal sesuai dengan harkat dan martabat kemanusiaan, serta mendapat perlindungan dari kekerasan dan diskriminasi.  
15. Perlindungan Khusus adalah suatu bentuk perlindungan yang diterima oleh Anak dalam situasi dan kondisi tertentu untuk mendapatkan jaminan rasa aman terhadap ancaman yang membahayakan diri dan jiwa dalam tumbuh kembangnya.  
16. Kekerasan adalah setiap perbuatan melawan hukum yang berakibat timbulnya kesengsaraan atau penderitaan secarafisik, seksual, mental, psikologis, termasuk penelantaran dan perlakuan buruk yang mengancamdan/atau membahayakan bagi jiwa dan raga serta merendahkan martabat.  
17. Perlindungan Khusus Anak adalah suatu bentuk perlindungan yang diterima oleh anak dalam situasi dan kondisi tertentu untuk mendapatkan jaminan rasa aman terhadap ancaman yang membahayakan diri dan jiwa dalam tubuh kembangnya.  
18. Anak dalam Situasi Darurat adalah Anak yang berada dalam situasi lingkungan yang mengancam dan mengganggu kehidupan dan penghidupan Anak yang -4- disebabkan, baik oleh faktor alam, nonalam, dan/ atau sosial.  
19. Anak yang Berhadapan dengan Hukum adalah Anak yang berkonflik dengan hukum, Anak yang menjadi korban tindak pidana, dan Anak yang menjadi saksi tindak pidana.  
20. Anak dari Kelompok Minoritas dan Terisolasi adalah Anak yang tertinggal, terdepan, terluar dalam lingkungan yang berbeda budaya, tradisi, suku, ras, agama dengan anak- anak lain yang jumlahnya jauh lebih sedikit dari Anak golongan lain.  
21. Anak yang Dieksploitasi secara Ekonomi adalah Anak yang menjadi korban dari tindakan pelacuran, kerja atau pelayanan paksa, perbudakan atau praktik serupa perbudakan, penindasan, pemerasan, pemanfaatan fisik, seksual, organ reproduksi, atau secara melawan hukummemindahkan atau mentransplantasi organ dan/atau jaringan tubuh atau memanfaatkan tenaga atau kemampuan Anak oleh pihak lain atau tindakan lain yang sejenis untuk mendapatkan keuntungan materiil.  
22. Anak yang Dieksploitasi secara Seksual adalah Anak yang dimanfaatkan untuk mendapatkan keuntungan melalui organ tubuh seksual atau organ tubuh lain dari Anak, termasuk tetapi tidak terbatas pada semua kegiatan pelacuran dan pencabulan.  
23. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Penyalahgunaan Narkotika, Alkohol, Psikotropika, dan Zat Adiktif Lainnya adalah Anak yang dibujuk, diperdaya, ditipu, dipaksa, dan/atau diancam untuk menggunakan narkotika, alkohol, psikotropika, dan zat adiktif lainnya.  
24. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Pornografi adalah Anak yang mengalami trauma atau penderitaan sebagai akibat tindak pidana pornografi.  
25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus yang selanjutnya disingkat HIV adalah virus yang menyerang sistem imun dan jika tidak diterapi dapat menurunkan daya tahan tubuh manusia hingga terjadi kondisi Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome.  
26. Acquired Immuno Deficiencg Syndrome yang selanjutnya disingkat AIDS adalah suatu kumpulan gejala berkurangnya kemampuan pertahanan diri yang disebabkan oleh masuknya virus HIV dalam tubuh seseorang.  
27. Anak dengan HIV dan AIDS adalah Anak yang terinfeksi HIV dan/atau AIDS baik tertular dari orang tua ataupun dari faktor risiko lainnya.  
28. Anak Korban Penculikan adalah Anak yang dibawa seseorang secara melawan hukum dengan maksud untuk menempatkan Anak tersebut di bawah kekuasaannya atau kekuasaan orang lain atau untuk menempatkan Anak dalam keadaan tidak berdaya.  
29. Anak Korban Penjualan adalah Anak yang dipindahtangankan oleh seseorang atau kelompok orang ke pihak lainnya untuk suatu imbalan atau alasan lainnya.  
30. Anak Korban Perdagangan adalah Anak yang mengalami penderitaan psikis, mental, fisik, seksual, ekonomi, dan/atau sosial yang diakibatkan tindakan perekrutan, pengangkutan, penampungan, pengiriman, pemindahan, atau penerimaan dengan ancaman kekerasan, penggunaan kekerasan, penculikan, penyekapan, pemalsuan, penipuan, penyalahgunaan kekuasaan atau posisi rentan, penjeratan utang atau memberi bayaran atau manfaat, sehingga memperoleh persetujuan dari orang yang memegang kendali atas orang lain tersebut, baik yang dilakukan di dalam negara maupun antarnegara, untuk tujuan eksploitasi atau mengakibatkan Anak tereksploitasi.  
31. Anak Korban Kekerasan Fisik adalah Anak yang mengalami kekerasan yang menimbulkan rasa sakit, jatuh sakit, atau luka berat.  
32. Anak Korban Kekerasan Psikis adalah Anak yang mengalami ketakutan, hilangnya rasa percaya diri, hilangnya kemampuan untuk bertindak, rasa tidak berdaya, dan/atau penderitaan psikis berat.  
33. Anak Korban Kejahatan Seksual adalah Anak yang mengalami pemaksaan hubungan seksual, pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan cara tidak wajar dan/atau tidak disukai, dan pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial dan I atau tujuan tertentu.  
34. Anak Korban Jaringan Terorisme adalah Anak yang mengalami penderitaan fisik, mental, dan/atau kerugian ekonomi yang disebabkan oleh tindak pidana terorisme baik sebagai Anak korban, Anak pelaku, Anak dari pelaku, dan Anak saksi.  
35. Anak Penyandang Disabilitas adalah Anak yang mengalami keterbatasan fisik, intelektual, mental, dan/atau sensorik dalam jangka waktu lama yang dalamberinteraksi dengan lingkungan dapat mengalami hambatan dan kesulitan untuk berpartisipasi secara penuh dan efektif berdasarkan kesamaan hak.  
36. Anak Korban Perlakuan Salah adalah Anak yang terancam secara fisik dan nonfisik karena tindak kekerasan, diperlakukan salah atau tidak semestinya dalam lingkungan keluarga atau lingkungan sosial terdekatnya, sehingga tidak terpenuhi kebutuhan dasarnya dengan wajar baik secara jasmani, rohani, maupun sosial.  
37. Anak Korban Penelantaran adalah Anak yang tidak mendapatkan pemenuhan kebutuhan seperti namun tidak terbatas pada kebutuhan kesehatan, keamanan, dan kesejahteraan dari orang tua atau orang lain yang memiliki tanggung jawab secara hukum untuk mengasuh Anak tersebut sehingga mengakibatkan kerugian dalamproses tumbuh kembang Anak.  
38. Anak dengan Perilaku Sosial Menyimpang adalah Anak yang bersikap dan berperilaku yang tidak mempertimbangkan penilaian dan keberadaan orang lain secara umum di sekitarnya, menunjukkan sikap tidak bertanggung jawab serta kurangnya penyesalan mengenai kesalahannya, dan sering melakukan pelanggaran hak dan norma yang hidup dalam masyarakat.  
39. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya adalah Anak yang diberikan label sosial negatif didasarkan pada prasangka dan bertujuan untuk memisahkan, membedakan, mendiskreditkan, dan mengucilkan Anak dengan cap atau pandangan buruk dari pelabelan terkait dengan kondisi orang tuanya.  
40. Keluarga Pengganti adalah orang tua asuh, orang tua angkat, dan wali yang menjalankan peran dan tanggung jawab untuk memberikan pengasuhan alternatif pada Anak.  
41. Lembaga Pendidikan adalah satuan pendidikan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam peraturan perundang- undangan mengenai sistem pendidikan nasional.  
42. Konseling adalah suatu proses yang dilakukan dalambentuk wawancara untuk membantu Anak memahami dirinya secara lebih baik, agar Anak dapat mengatasi kesulitan dalam penyesuaian dirinya terhadap berbagai peranan dan relasi serta menemukan pemecahan permasalahan yang tepat.  
43. Pendampingan Sosial adalah interaksi dinamis antara pekerja sosial dengan Anak yang memerlukan Perlindungan Khusus untuk bersama-sama menghadapi dan memecahkan masalah sosial yang dihadapi.  
44. Rehabilitasi Sosial adalah proses refungsionalisasi dan pengembangan untuk memungkinkan Anak mampu melaksanakan fungsi sosialnya secara wajar dalamkehidupan masyarakat.  
45. Reintegrasi Sosial adalah proses penyiapan Anak yang memerlukan Perlindungan Khusus untuk dapat kembali ke lingkungan keluarga dan masyarakat.  
46. Pemenuhan Hak Anak yang selanjutnya disingkat PHA adalah strategi perlindungan anak dengan mengintegrasikan hak anak ke dalam setiap kegiatan pembangunan yang sejak penyusunan perencanaan, penganggaran, pelaksanaan, pemantauan, dan evaluasi dari berbagai peraturan perundang-undangan, kebijakan, program, dan kegiatan dengan menerapkan prinsip kepentingan terbaik bagi anak.  
47. Diskriminasi adalah setiap pembatasan, pelecehan, atau pengucilan, yang secara langsung atau tidak langsung -7- didasarkan pada pembedaan pada manusia atas dasar, agama, suku, ras, golongan, status sosial, status ekonomi, jenis kelamin, bahasa, keyakinan politik, status hukum anak, dan kondisi fisik dan/atau mental yang berakibat pengurangan, penyimpangan, atau penghapusan, pengakuan, pelaksanaan atau penggunaan hak asasi manusia dan kebebasan dasar dalamkehidupan baik individual maupun kolektif dalam bidang politik, ekonomi, hukum, sosial budaya dan aspek kehidupan lainnya.  
48. Eksploitasi adalah tindakan dengan atau tanpa persetujuan korban yang meliputi tetapi tidak terbatas pada pelacuran, kerja atau pelayanan paksa, perbudakan atau praktik serupa perbudakan, penindasan, pemerasan, pemanfaatan fisik seksual, organ reproduksi atau secara melawan hukum memindahkan atau mentransplatasikan organ dan/atau jaringan tubuh atau memanfaatkan tenaga atau kemampuan seseorang oleh pihak lain untuk mendapatkan keuntungan baik materiil maupun immateriil.  
49. Orangtua adalah ayah dan/atau ibu kandung, atau ayah dan/atau ibu tiri, atau ayah dan/atau ibu angkat.  
50. Wali adalah orang atau badan yang dalam kenyataannya menjalankan kekuasaan asuh sebagai orang tua terhadap anak.  
51. Keluarga adalah unit terkecil dalam masyarakat yang terdiri dari suami isteri dan anaknya, atau ayah dan anaknya, atau ibu dan anaknya, atau keluarga sedarah dalam garis lurus ke atas atau ke bawah sampai dengan derajat ketiga.  
52. Masyarakat adalah perseorangan, keluarga, kelompok dan organisasi sosial dan/atau organisasi kemasyarakatan, dunia usaha.

# CHAPTER I

## GENERAL PROVISIONS

#### Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:  
1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu.  
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.  
6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.  
7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically built to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy.  
8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region.  
9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women.  
10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice.  
11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.  
12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.  
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.  
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.  
15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.  
16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.  
17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.  
18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.  
19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.  
20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than other groups of Children.  
21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.  
22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.  
23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.  
24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.  
25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the human immune system until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs.  
26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body.  
27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.  
28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state.  
29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons.  
30. Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.  
31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.  
32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.  
33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.  
34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses.  
35. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.  
36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.  
37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process.  
38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that exist in society.  
39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to their parents' condition.  
40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children.  
41. Educational Institution is an educational unit as referred to in laws and regulations concerning the national education system.  
42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find appropriate problem solutions.  
43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems faced.  
44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to carry out their social functions properly in community life.  
45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment.  
46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child.  
47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, which directly or indirectly -7- is based on differentiation among humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.  
48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits.  
49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.  
50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.  
51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.  
52. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

# BAB II

## PEMBERDAYAAN PEREMPUAN

## Bagian Kesatu

Umum

#### Pasal 2

1. Pemberdayaan perempuan di Kabupaten dilaksanakan melalui perlindungan hak perempuan.  
2. Pemberdayaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan dalam rangka memenuhi hak perempuan dalam meningkatkan kualitas hidup perempuan.  
3. Hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) wajib dijamin oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten.  
4. Hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (3) meliputi bidang pendidikan, bidang kesehatan, bidang ketenagakerjaan, bidang politik, bidang hukum, bidang ekonomi budaya dan sosial.

## Bagian Kedua

Kewajiban Pemerintah Kabupaten

#### Pasal 3

1. Pemerintah Kabupaten wajib menjamin perlindungan hak perempuan.  
2. Perlindungan hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan dengan:  
a. penyusunan kebijakan daerah yang responsif gender;  
b. pelembagaan PUG di lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten;  
c. pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang pendidikan, bidang kesehatan, bidang ketenagakerjaan, bidang politik, bidang hukum, bidang ekonomi budaya dan social pada organisasi kemasyarakatan tingkat Kabupaten; dan  
d. penguatan dan pengembangan lembaga penyedia layanan pemberdayaan perempuan tingkat kabupaten.

#### Pasal 4

1. Penyusunan kebijakan Kabupaten yang responsif gender sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf a menjadi pedoman dalam penyusunan rencana pembangunan daerah.  
2. Penyusunan rencana pembangunan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi rencana jangka panjang, rencana jangka menengah, dan rencana kerja pemerintah daerah.  
3. Rencana pembangunan jangka panjang, rencana jangka menengah, dan rencana kerja pemerintah daerah sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) harus menjadi pedoman PD dalam penyusunan rencana strategis dan rencana kerja di lingkungan kerja masing-masing.  
4. Penyusunan Rencana pembangunan sebagaimana dimaksud pad ayat (3) dilakukan melalui perencanaan yang responsif gender melalui analisis gender dan ARG yang memuat skala prioritas pelaksanaan pemberdayaan perempuan.  
5. Penyusunan skala prioritas pelaksanaan pemberdayaan perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (4) berpedoman pada skala prioritas tingkat nasional.  
6. Skala prioritas tingkat nasional sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (5) menjadi bagian yang tidak terpisahkan dalamrencana pembangunan daerah.

#### Pasal 5

Dalam rangka menjamin terwujudnya penyusunan kebijakan yang responsif gender sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf a, PD yang melaksanakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang perencanaan pembangunan daerah wajib:  
a. melibatkan PD yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang pemberdayaan perempuan dalamperumusan rencana pembangunan daerah; dan  
b. mengevaluasi program dan kegiatan di tingkat PD yangtidak responsif gender.

#### Pasal 6

1. Pelembagaan PUG sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf b dilaksanakan di seluruh PD di lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten.  
2. Untuk mempercepat pelembagaan PUG sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), Bupati dapat membentuk Kelompok Kerja PUG tingkat Kabupaten.  
3. Anggota Pokja PUG sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) adalah seluruh Kepala/Pimpinan PD.  
4. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tugas dan tata cara keanggotaan Pokja PUG diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

#### Pasal 7

1. Dalam rangka penguatan dan pengembangan PUG, Bupati dapat membentuk Focal Point PUG.  
2. Focal Point PUG sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) adalah aparatur PD yang mempunyai kemampuan untuk melakukan pengarusutamaan gender di unit kerjanya masing-masing.  
3. Focal Point sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dibentukpada setiap PD.  
4. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tugas, susunan keanggotaan dan tata cara pembentukan Focal Point dilaksanakan sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.

#### Pasal 8

Pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang pendidikan, bidang kesehatan, bidang ketenagakerjaan, bidang politik, bidang hukum, bidang ekonomi budaya dan sosial pada organisasi kemasyarakatan tingkat Kabupaten sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf c merupakan bagian dari kebijakan khusus sementara yang diberikan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten.

#### Pasal 9

Pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang pendidikan dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi perempuan untuk memperoleh pendidikan dan pengajaran disemua jenis, jenjang dan jalur pendidikan sesuai dengan persyaratan yang telah ditentukan;  
b. kebijakan pendidikan sudah mendorong untuk terjadinya pemerataan, peningkatan dan mutu relevansi pendidikan untuk semua jenis kelamin; dan  
c. pemerataan kesempatan belajar bagi Perempuan dan laki laki.

#### Pasal 10

Pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang kesehatan dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi kesehatan perempuan melalui programkegiatan kesehatan yang dilaksanakan pemerintahan seperti:
1\. Program penurunan angka kematian ibu;  
2\. Program kesehatan ibu dan anak (KIA);  
3\. Program lingkungan sehat, penyehatan air dan sanitasi;  
4\. Program pemberantasan penyakit malaria;  
5\. Program pemberantasan penyakit tuberkulosis paru;  
6\. Program penanggulangan HIV/AIDS;  
7\. Program perbaikan gizi masyarakat;  
b. Perempuan diberikan hak untuk mendapatkan perlindungan khusus dalam pelaksanaan pekerjaan atau profesinya terhadap hal-hal yang dapat mengancamkeselamataan dan/atau kesehatannya;  
c. Perempuan dieberikan hak khusus yang melekat padaa diri wanita dikarenakan fungsi reproduksinya, dijamin dan dilindungi oleh hukum.

#### Pasal 11

Pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang ketenagakerjaan dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. pengupahan sama bagi buruh laki-laki dan perempuan untuk pekerjaan yang sama;  
b. larangan diskriminasi bagi pekerja wanita;  
c. larangan PHK bagi pekerja perempuan yang menikah, hamil, dan melahirkan;  
d. pedoman mempekerjakan pekerja perempuan malam hari;  
e. memberikan keleluasaan bagi pekerja perempuan yang menyusui anak;  
f. larangan diskriminasi bagi pekerja perempuan dalamperaturan perusahaan; dan  
g. tentang kekurangan gizi pada pekerja perempuan.

#### Pasal 12

Pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang politik dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi peningkatan sumber daya manusia kepada bakal calon anggota legislatif tingkat kabupaten, dan anggota partai politik/organisasi masyarakat perempuan dalam rangka memenuhi keterwakilan perempuan di lembaga legislatif sesuai dengan peraturan perundang- undangan;  
b. memfasilitasi peningkatan partisipasi politik perempuan di lembaga legislatif;  
c. memberikan sarana dan prasarana bagi organisasi masyarakat perempuan atau organisasi masyarakat yang visi misinya memperjuangkan pemenuhan hak dan perlindungan perempuan di Kabupaten sesuai dengan kemampuan Keuangan Daerah;  
d. melaksanakan sosialisasi dalam rangka meningkatkan kesadaran atas hak perempuan dan partisipasi perempuan di bidang politik;  
e. mendorong peningkatan keterlibatan perempuan dalamorganisasi kemasyarakatan dan kegiatan pengambilan keputusan di lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten; dan  
f. mendorong pembentukan organisasi/forum perempuan.

#### Pasal 13

Pemberdayaan perempuan dalam bidang hukumdilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi peningkatan pengetahuan dan kesadaran hukum bagi perempuan; dan  
b. mendorong pembentukan organisasi yang memberikan layanan hukum secara gratis bagi perempuan.

#### Pasal 14

1. Pemberdayaan perempuan dalam bidang ekonomi dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi perempuan dalam usaha meningkatkan perekonomian keluarga;  
b. dapat memberikan bantuan permodalan kepada perempuan, terutama buruh migran, perempuan di daerah terpencil, perempuansebagai kepala rumah tangga, dan perempuan korban kekerasan dalamrumah tangga; dan  
c. melaksanakan program pengembangan industri rumah tangga dan industri nonpertanian.  
2. Tata cara pemberian bantuan permodalan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) huruf b diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

# CHAPTER II

## WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

## Part One

General

#### Article 2

1. Women's empowerment in the Regency is implemented through the protection of women's rights.  
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to fulfill women's rights in improving the quality of women's lives.  
3. Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (2) must be guaranteed by the Regency Government.  
4. Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) include the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture and social.

## Part Two

Obligations of the Regency Government

#### Article 3

1. The Regency Government is obliged to guarantee the protection of women's rights.  
2. Protection of women's rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:  
a. formulation of gender-responsive regional policies;  
b. institutionalization of PUG within the Regency Government;  
c. women's empowerment in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture and social in community organizations at the Regency level; and  
d. strengthening and development of women's empowerment service provider institutions at the regency level.

#### Article 4

1. The formulation of gender-responsive Regency policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a shall serve as a guideline in the preparation of regional development plans.  
2. The preparation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (1) includes long-term plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans.  
3. Long-term development plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans as referred to in paragraph (2) must serve as guidelines for PD in the preparation of strategic plans and work plans within their respective work environments.  
4. The preparation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (3) is carried out through gender-responsive planning through gender analysis and ARG which contains a priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment.  
5. The preparation of priority scales for the implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (4) is guided by the national level priority scale.  
6. The national level priority scale as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be an inseparable part of the regional development plan.

#### Article 5

In order to ensure the realization of the formulation of gender-responsive policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a, PD that carries out governmental affairs in the field of regional development planning is obliged to:  
a. involve PD that carries out governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment in the formulation of regional development plans; and  
b. evaluate programs and activities at the PD level that are not gender-responsive.

#### Article 6

1. The institutionalization of PUG as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter b is implemented in all PD within the Regency Government.  
2. To accelerate the institutionalization of PUG as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may establish a PUG Working Group at the Regency level.  
3. Members of the PUG Pokja as referred to in paragraph (2) are all Heads/Leaders of PD.  
4. Further provisions regarding the duties and procedures for membership of the PUG Pokja are regulated by Regent Regulation.

#### Article 7

1. In order to strengthen and develop PUG, the Regent may establish a PUG Focal Point.  
2. The PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) is a PD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.  
3. The Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) is established in each PD.  
4. Further provisions regarding the duties, membership composition and procedures for establishing the Focal Point are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 8

Women's empowerment in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture and social in community organizations at the Regency level as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter c constitutes part of temporary special policies provided by the Regency Government.

#### Article 9

Women's empowerment in the field of education is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating women to obtain education and teaching in all types, levels and pathways of education in accordance with predetermined requirements;  
b. education policies have encouraged equity, improvement and quality relevance of education for all genders; and  
c. equal learning opportunities for women and men.

#### Article 10

Women's empowerment in the field of health is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating women's health through health program activities implemented by the government such as:
1\. Maternal mortality reduction program;  
2\. Maternal and child health (KIA) program;  
3\. Healthy environment, water sanitation and sanitation program;  
4\. Malaria eradication program;  
5\. Pulmonary tuberculosis eradication program;  
6\. HIV/AIDS prevention program;  
7\. Community nutrition improvement program;  
b. Women are given the right to obtain special protection in the implementation of their work or profession against matters that may threaten their safety and/or health;  
c. Women are given special rights inherent to women due to their reproductive function, guaranteed and protected by law.

#### Article 11

Women's empowerment in the field of employment is implemented by means including:  
a. equal wages for male and female workers for the same work;  
b. prohibition of discrimination against female workers;  
c. prohibition of termination of employment for female workers who marry, become pregnant, and give birth;  
d. guidelines for employing female workers at night;  
e. providing flexibility for female workers who breastfeed children;  
f. prohibition of discrimination against female workers in company regulations; and  
g. regarding malnutrition in female workers.

#### Article 12

Women's empowerment in the field of politics is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating the improvement of human resources for prospective legislative candidates at the regency level, and members of political parties/women's community organizations in order to fulfill women's representation in legislative institutions in accordance with laws and regulations;  
b. facilitating the increase of women's political participation in legislative institutions;  
c. providing facilities and infrastructure for women's community organizations or community organizations whose vision and mission is to fight for the fulfillment of rights and protection of women in the Regency in accordance with Regional Financial capacity;  
d. implementing socialization in order to increase awareness of women's rights and women's participation in the field of politics;  
e. encouraging increased involvement of women in community organizations and decision-making activities within the Regency Government; and  
f. encouraging the establishment of women's organizations/forums.

#### Article 13

Women's empowerment in the field of law is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating the improvement of legal knowledge and awareness for women; and  
b. encouraging the establishment of organizations that provide free legal services for women.

#### Article 14

1. Women's empowerment in the field of economy is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating women in efforts to improve family economy;  
b. may provide capital assistance to women, especially migrant workers, women in remote areas, women as heads of households, and women victims of domestic violence; and  
c. implementing home industry and non-agricultural industry development programs.  
2. Procedures for providing capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Pemberdayaan perempuan dalam bidang budaya dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi perempuan dalam melestarikan kebudayaan asli daerah;  
b. mendorong aktivitas perempuan dalam berbagai kegiatan seni budaya.

#### Pasal 16

Pemberdayaan perempuan dalam bidang sosial dilaksanakan dengan cara antara lain:  
a. memfasilitasi perempuan dalam peningkatan aktivitas sosial di lingkungan masyarakat; dan  
b. mendorong aktivitas perempuan sebagai agen perubahanpada masyarakat.

## Bagian Ketiga

Ruang Lingkup Pemberdayaan Perempuan

### Paragraf 1

Umum

#### Pasal 17

Perlindungan Perempuan dilakukan dengan cara:  
a. pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan;  
b. penyediaan layanan dan penanganan rujukan lanjutan; dan  
c. penguatan dan pengembangan lembaga penyedia layanan perlindungan perempuan.

### Paragraf 2

Pencegahan

#### Pasal 18

1. Pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 17 huruf a dilaksanakan dengan cara meningkatkan kesadaran keluarga dan masyarakat.  
2. Peningkatan kesadaran keluarga dan masyarakat sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan secara terpadu dan berkesinambungan dalam bentuk sosialisasi, bimbingan dan pelatihan, dan/atau penyuluhan.
3. Sosialisasi, bimbingan dan pelatihan, dan/atau penyuluhan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) dilaksanakan oleh PD teknis yang membidangi, lembaga, organisasi, media masa, dunia usaha, akademisi, penegak hukum, masyarakat dan Unit Pelaksana Teknis Daerah sesuai dengan tugas dan fungsinya.

#### Pasal 19

1. Selain pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 18, upaya pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan dilakukan dengan meningkatkan wawasan, pengetahuan, keterampilan, dan kemandirian perempuan.  
2. Pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan dengan cara:  
a. meningkatkan pendidikan informal;  
b. membuka aksesibilitas untuk memperoleh pendidikan, pelatihan, pendanaan, peningkatan pendapatan, dan pelayanan sosial; dan  
c. menyediakan akses lapangan kerja informal bagi perempuan.

### Paragraf 3

Penyediakan Layanan dan Penanganan Rujukan Lanjutan

#### Pasal 20

Penyediaan layanan dan penanganan rujukan lanjutan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 17 huruf b diperuntukkan bagi:  
a. perempuan korban kekerasan dalam rumah tangga;  
b. perempuan korban tindak pidana perdagangan orang;  
c. perempuan dalam situasi darurat dan kondisi khusus; dan  
d. perempuan korban tindak kekerasan lainnya yang memerlukan koordinasi tingkat Kabupaten.

#### Pasal 21

1. Selain penyediaan layanan dan penanganan rujukan layanan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 20, Pemerintah Kabupaten wajib menyediakan layanan khusus bagi:  
a. perempuan yang termasuk dalam kelompok rentan dan/atau minoritas;  
b. perempuan lanjut usia; dan  
c. perempuan berkebutuhan khusus.  
2. Layanan khusus sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diberikan dalam bentuk:  
a. kemudahan dalam memperoleh dan menikmati haknya sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang- undangan;  
b. kemudahan dalam akses terhadap sumber daya ekonomi dan sumber daya alam, jaminan sosial, dan pelayanandasar publik; dan  
c. penyediaan kebutuhan spesifik perempuan dalamsituasidarurat dan kondisi khusus.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai layanan khusus sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

#### Pasal 22

1. Dalam rangka penyediaan layanan dan penanganan rujukan lanjutan bagi perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 20, Pemerintah Kabupaten dapat membentuk:  
a. unit Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak (PPA) tingkat Kabupaten;  
b. gugus tugas; dan/atau  
c. satuan tugas.  
2. Unit PPA, gugus tugas, dan/atau satuan tugas sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dibentuk dengan Peraturan Bupati.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tugas, keanggotaan, tatacara dan/atau satuan tugas kerja unit PPA sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

### Paragraf 4

Penguatan dan Pengembangan Lembaga Penyedia Layanan Perlindungan Perempuan

#### Pasal 23

Penguatan lembaga penyedia layanan perlindungan perempuan dilakukan dengan:  
a. pembentukan forum koordinasi atau forum lainnya dalamrangka mendukung penanganan korban kekerasan terhadap perempuan;  
b. penyediaan unit layanan dan pendampingan perlindungan hukum bagi perempuan korban kekerasan yang melakukan pendataan terkait kekerasan terhadap perempuan;  
c. penyediaan komunikasi informasi edukasi, advokasi, sosialisasi, dan bimbingan teknis;  
d. pengadaan sarana dan prasarana perlindungan danpelayanan perempuan di wilayah bencana dan pengungsian;  
e. peningkatan koordinasi lintas sektor;  
f. pembentukan kelompok kerja;  
g. penyusunan rencana aksi daerah; dan  
h. komunikasi informasi edukasi baik melalui media elektronik maupun cetak dan simulasi tentang perlindungan perempuan.

# BAB III

## PENYELENGGARAAN PERLINDUNGAN ANAK

## Bagian Kesatu

Umum

#### Pasal 24

1. Dalam rangka pelaksanaan Perlindungan Anak, Pemerintah Kabupaten berkewajiban melakukan kegiatan:  
a. perumusan kebijakan, program, dan kegiatan pembangunan daerah yang berwawasan hak anak yang dituangkan dalam dokumen perencanaan pembangunan daerah;  
b. perumusan norma, standar prosedur dan kriteriapenilaian pemenuhan dan perlindungan hak anak yang mengacu pada norma, standar, prosedur dan kriteria yang ditetapkan Pemerintah;  
c. koordinasi pengembangan Kabupaten layak anak dilaksanakansesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang- undangan;  
d. fasilitasi terselenggaranya forum anak daerah;  
e. peningkatan peran serta Masyarakat dalampenyelenggaraan dan perlindungan hak anak;  
f. koordinasi dan kerja sama dalam pemenuhan dan perlindungan Anak;  
g. monitoring dan evaluasi terhadap pelaksanaan programpemenuhan dan perlindungan Anak;  
h. pembinaan lembaga perlindungan anak; dan i. memberikan perlindungan khusus bagi Anak.  
2. Selain kegiatan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), Pemerintah Kabupaten dapat melakukan pengawasan dan fasilitasi terhadap lembaga advokasi anak di Kabupaten yang terlibat di dalam pendampingan terhadap Anak yang memerlukan penanganan khusus.  
3. Pengawasan dan fasilitasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) dilaksanakan sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.  
4. Pemberian fasilitasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (3) disesuaikan dengan kemampuan keuangan daerah.

#### Pasal 25

1. Koordinasi pengembangan kabupaten layak anak sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 24 ayat (1) huruf c dilaksanakan untuk mendorong percepatan terwujudnya kabupaten Layak Anak.  
2. Koordinasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan oleh instansi terkait sesuai tugas pokok dan fungsinya.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai bentuk dan tata cara koordinasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diatur dalam Peraturan Bupati.

#### Pasal 26

1. Pembinaan lembaga perlindungan Anak sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 24 ayat (1) huruf h dilaksanakan dalam rangka meningkatkan efektivitas penyelanggaraan pemenuhan hak anak.  
2. Pembinaan lembaga perlindungan Anak sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan oleh Kepala PD yang tugas dan fungsinya menyelenggarakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang perlindungan anak.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai pembinaan danpengembangan kelembagaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diatur dalam Peraturan Bupati.

#### Pasal 27

Kegiatan dalan Penyelenggaraan Perlindungan anak di Kabupaten meliputi:  
a. pemenuhan hak anak; dan  
b. perlindungan khusus anak.

## Bagian Kedua

Pemenuhan Hak Anak

#### Pasal 28

Pemenuhan hak anak menjadi kewajiban Pemerintah Kabupaten, Orangtua, dan masyarakat.

#### Article 15

Empowerment of women in the field of culture is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating women in preserving the original regional culture;  
b. encouraging women's activities in various cultural and artistic activities.

#### Article 16

Empowerment of women in the social field is implemented by means including:  
a. facilitating women in increasing social activities in the community environment; and  
b. encouraging women's activities as agents of change in society.

## Part Three

Scope of Women's Empowerment

### Paragraph 1

General

#### Article 17

Protection of Women is carried out by means of:  
a. prevention of violence against women;  
b. provision of services and further referral handling; and  
c. strengthening and development of institutions providing women's protection services.

### Paragraph 2

Prevention

#### Article 18

1. Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by means of increasing family and community awareness.  
2. Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.
3. Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented by technical Regional Apparatus responsible for the field, institutions, organizations, mass media, business sector, academics, law enforcement, the community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

#### Article 19

1. In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by increasing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.  
2. Prevention of violence against women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by means of:  
a. increasing informal education;  
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement, and social services; and  
c. providing access to informal employment for women.

### Paragraph 3

Provision of Services and Further Referral Handling

#### Article 20

Provision of services and further referral handling as referred to in Article 17 letter b is intended for:  
a. women victims of domestic violence;  
b. women victims of trafficking in persons;  
c. women in emergency situations and special conditions; and  
d. women victims of other acts of violence requiring coordination at the Regency level.

#### Article 21

1. In addition to the provision of services and referral service handling as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government is obliged to provide special services for:  
a. women who are included in vulnerable and/or minority groups;  
b. elderly women; and  
c. women with special needs.  
2. Special services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided in the form of:  
a. ease in obtaining and enjoying their rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;  
b. ease in access to economic resources and natural resources, social security, and basic public services; and  
c. provision of specific needs of women in emergency situations and special conditions.  
3. Further provisions regarding special services as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

#### Article 22

1. In the context of providing services and further referral handling for women as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government may establish:  
a. a Women and Children Protection (PPA) unit at the Regency level;  
b. a task force; and/or  
c. a working unit.  
2. The PPA unit, task force, and/or working unit as referred to in paragraph (1) are established by Regent Regulation.  
3. Further provisions regarding the duties, membership, procedures and/or working unit of the PPA unit as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

### Paragraph 4

Strengthening and Development of Institutions Providing Women's Protection Services

#### Article 23

Strengthening of institutions providing women's protection services is carried out by:  
a. establishment of a coordination forum or other forums in order to support the handling of victims of violence against women;  
b. provision of service units and legal protection assistance for women victims of violence who conduct data collection related to violence against women;  
c. provision of information education communication, advocacy, socialization, and technical guidance;  
d. procurement of facilities and infrastructure for protection and services for women in disaster and evacuation areas;  
e. improvement of cross-sectoral coordination;  
f. establishment of working groups;  
g. formulation of regional action plans; and  
h. information education communication both through electronic and print media and simulations regarding women's protection.

# CHAPTER III

## IMPLEMENTATION OF CHILD PROTECTION

## Part One

General

#### Article 24

1. In the context of implementing Child Protection, the Regency Government is obliged to carry out activities:  
a. formulation of policies, programs, and regional development activities with a child rights perspective which are set forth in regional development planning documents;  
b. formulation of norms, standard procedures and assessment criteria for the fulfillment and protection of children's rights which refer to the norms, standards, procedures and criteria established by the Government;  
c. coordination of child-friendly Regency development is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;  
d. facilitation of the implementation of regional children's forums;  
e. enhancement of Community participation in the implementation and protection of children's rights;  
f. coordination and cooperation in the fulfillment and protection of Children;  
g. monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of programs for the fulfillment and protection of Children;  
h. guidance of child protection institutions; and i. provision of special protection for Children.  
2. In addition to the activities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regency Government may conduct supervision and facilitation of child advocacy institutions in the Regency involved in assistance to Children requiring special handling.  
3. Supervision and facilitation as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
4. Provision of facilitation as referred to in paragraph (3) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity.

#### Article 25

1. Coordination of child-friendly regency development as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter c is implemented to encourage acceleration of the realization of a Child-Friendly Regency.  
2. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by relevant agencies in accordance with their main duties and functions.  
3. Further provisions regarding the form and procedures for coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

#### Article 26

1. Guidance of Child protection institutions as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter h is implemented in order to increase the effectiveness of the implementation of the fulfillment of children's rights.  
2. Guidance of Child protection institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Head of the Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are to administer government affairs in the field of child protection.  
3. Further provisions regarding guidance and institutional development as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

#### Article 27

Activities in the Implementation of Child Protection in the Regency include:  
a. fulfillment of children's rights; and  
b. special protection of children.

## Part Two

Fulfillment of Children's Rights

#### Article 28

Fulfillment of children's rights is the obligation of the Regency Government, Parents, and the community.

b. rehabilitasi Sosial;

Anak yang Menjadi Korban Penyalahgunaan Narkotika, Alkohol, Psikotropika, dan Zatadiktif Lainnya

Special protection for children from minority and isolated groups as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter c shall be carried out through the provision of facilities and infrastructure to enable them to enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and -26- practice their own religion, and use their own language.

#### Article 42

1. The provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out in the form of:  
a. provision of culture-based public spaces, art and culture centers, along with equipment and training including places of worship;  
b. provision of facilities required in providing services for Children from minority and isolated groups; and  
c. provision of accessibility required by Children from minority and isolated groups to obtain fulfillment of basic needs.  
3. In the event that Children from minority and isolated groups experience trauma as a result of violence, discrimination and other mistreatment, social rehabilitation, medical services, and/or mental health services shall be provided.

#### Article 43

1. Special Protection for Children from Minority and Isolated Groups so that they do not experience violence, discrimination, and other mistreatment as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out through preventive measures.  
2. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:a. provision of education to the community;and b. coordination with the Regency Government.  c. preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
3. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 4

Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually

#### Article 44

Special Protection for Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out through:  
a. dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations -27- relating to the protection of Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually;  
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and  
c. involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children economically and/or sexually.

#### Article 45

1. Dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations as referred to in Article 44 letter a shall be carried out through:  
a. legal counseling; and  
b. communication, information, and education facilities.  
3. Dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.

#### Article 46

1. Monitoring as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be carried out by means of observation, identification, and recording to obtain data and information related to the condition of:a. children Who Are Exploited Economically; or b. children Who Are Exploited Sexually.  
2. Monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Economically as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out at economic center locations and outside economic centers.  
3. Monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Sexually as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out through supervision of:  
a. prostitution and solicitation practices in the environment;  
b. locations suspected of being places of sexual exploitation of Children;  
c. perpetrators suspected of sexually exploiting Children; and  
d. raid actions to free Children from sexual exploitation.  
4. Monitoring and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.  
5. Reporting as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be prepared after monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually has been carried out.  
6. Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 44 -28- letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 47

Involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 44 letter c shall be carried out through:  
a. formulation of policies on the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children in their environment;  
b. cooperation to prevent Children from being exploited economically and/or sexually;  
c. campaigns for the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children;  
d. increased supervision to prevent Children from being exploited economically and/or sexually;  
e. company support for the elimination of exploitation of Children through corporate social responsibility; and  
f. reporting to the competent authorities if there is exploitation of Children economically and/or sexually.

#### Article 48

In the event that Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually require restoration of their condition to its original state, services must be provided in the form of:  
a. medical rehabilitation;  
b. Social rehabilitation;  
c. legal assistance and social assistance; and/or  
d. repatriation and Social Reintegration.

### Paragraph 5

Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse

#### Article 49

Special Protection for Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter e shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts.

#### Article 50

Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out by means of: -29-
a. strengthening of families and the Community so that Children are no longer involved in the abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
b. monitoring in the surrounding environment to prevent the circulation or abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and  
c. reporting to competent officials/agencies if circulation and abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances occur.

#### Article 51

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out through:  
a. communication, information, and education about the dangers for Children if involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
b. enhancement of the role of parents, families, the Community, educators, education personnel, religious leaders, customary leaders, Community leaders in supporting the Social Reintegration process of Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse;  
c. provision of understanding and awareness to Children regarding the dangers of smoking;  
d. provision of understanding and awareness to Children about the dangers of Children being involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
e. involvement of Children as peers in order to provide understanding and change in mindset about the dangers of Children being involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and  
f. inclusion of anti-narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances teaching materials in educational units.

#### Article 52

1. Treatment efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out to provide recovery of the physical and psychological condition of Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse.  
2. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:  
a. outpatient care;  
b. initial inpatient care;  
c. continued care; and  
d. post-care.

#### Article 53

Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out through medical rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, and post-rehabilitation.

#### Article 54

1. Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 50 shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
2. Care efforts as referred to in Article 52 and Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 53 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 6

Children who are Victims of Pornography

#### Article 55

1. Special Protection for Children who are Victims of Pornography as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter f shall be implemented through guidance, assistance, and social, physical and mental health recovery efforts.  
2. Provisions regarding guidance, assistance, social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 56

Guidance as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its authority by:  
a. coordinating the prevention and handling of Child pornography;  
b. conducting socialization;  
c. organizing education and training;  
d. increasing public awareness and responsibility; and  
e. conducting guidance through institutional and non-institutional systems.

#### Article 57

Assistance as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be implemented through:  
a. guidance and Counseling; and  
b. other necessary activities.

#### Article 58

Social recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:  
a. resocialization;  
b. counseling on moral values sourced from religious teachings in accordance with the religion professed by the Child;  
c. increasing public awareness to be able to re-accept Children who are victims or perpetrators of pornography; and  
d. periodic monitoring.

#### Article 59

Physical and mental health recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:  
a. psychosocial therapy;  
b. counseling;  
c. beneficial activities;  
d. referral to hospitals, safe houses, service centers, or other alternative places according to needs; and/or  
e. resocialization.

#### Article 60

1. Where necessary, the Regency Government and the Community may undertake prevention efforts so that Children do not become victims of pornography.  
2. Prevention efforts by the Regency Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:  
a. formulation and implementation of policies related to regional action plans on the prevention and handling of pornography;  
b. optimization of the role of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Pornography;  
c. capacity building of the Regional Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Pornography;  
d. formulation and dissemination of communication, information, and education materials related to the prevention of pornography in schools and the Community;  
e. guidance to the Community not to engage in activities leading to pornography; and  
f. guidance to Regional Apparatus, non-governmental organizations, and the Community to enhance prevention and handling efforts for pornography.  
3. Prevention efforts by the Community so that Children do not become Victims of Pornography shall be through:  
a. dissemination of communication, information, and education materials related to the prevention of pornography in the surrounding environment;  
b. strengthening the surrounding environment not to engage in activities leading to pornography; and  
c. enhancing prevention and handling efforts for pornography in the surrounding environment.  
4. Provisions regarding the procedures for prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

#### Article 61

1. Guidance and assistance as referred to in Article 53 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its authority.  
2. Social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 7

Children with HIV and AIDS

#### Article 62

Special Protection for Children with HIV and AIDS as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter g shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, care, and rehabilitation efforts.

#### Article 63

Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 62 shall be carried out in the form of:  
a. periodic or ad hoc examinations as well as integrated examinations of Children with HIV and AIDS;  
b. testing of periodic and/or ad hoc reports related to the prevention, handling, and protection of Children from HIV and AIDS;  
c. health surveillance in the form of recording, reporting, and data analysis on mothers, pregnant mothers, or Children indicated with HIV; and  
d. monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of prevention, handling, and protection of Children from HIV and AIDS.

#### Article 64

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 62 shall be carried out in the form of:  
a. formulating and implementing policies related to action plans on the prevention and handling of Children with HIV and AIDS;  
b. health promotion to increase public knowledge about the benefits of early detection and transmission of HIV and AIDS as well as increasing the knowledge and responsibility of mothers, pregnant mothers, Children, and married couples;  
c. preventing the transmission of HIV and AIDS from mother to Child;  
d. preventing Children from using narcotics;  
e. early detection by providing HIV and AIDS tests to pregnant mothers in areas with widespread and concentrated HIV and AIDS endemics;  
f. early detection by providing HIV and AIDS tests to pregnant mothers with sexually transmitted infections and tuberculosis in areas with low HIV epidemics;  
g. using sterile medical equipment for Children to avoid HIV and AIDS;  
h. avoiding blood transfusions contaminated with HIV and AIDS to Children;  
i. providing information about the transmission of HIV and AIDS to Children;  
j. changing Children's behavior to avoid HIV and AIDS;  
k. keeping Children away from tattooing; and  
l. establishing communication, consultation, and information centers about HIV and AIDS at the village level.

#### Article 65

1. Treatment as referred to in Article 62 shall be carried out to:  
a. reduce or inhibit the development of the HIV and AIDS virus in Children;  
b. reduce the risk of HIV and AIDS transmission;  
c. reduce or inhibit the worsening of opportunistic infections; and  
d. improve the quality of life of Children with HIV and AIDS.  
3. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 66

1. Care as referred to in Article 62 must be implemented with an approach chosen according to needs:  
a. care based on health service facilities; and  
b. Community-based home care.  
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 67

1. Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 62 is aimed at restoring the quality of life of Children to become productive.  
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through assistance, regular and correct medication consumption, health psychology Counseling, and Social Reintegration.  
3. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for every pattern of HIV transmission in Children.

#### Article 68

The Regency Government is obligated to seek equality in access, participation, and benefits in life for Children with HIV and AIDS.

#### Article 69

1. Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 63 shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 64 and Treatment, care, and rehabilitation as referred to in Article 65 through Article 67 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 8

Child Victims of Abduction, Sale, and/or Trafficking

#### Article 70

Special Protection for Child Victims of Abduction, Sale, and/or Trafficking as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter h shall be carried out through -35- supervision, protection, prevention, care, and rehabilitation.

### Paragraph 11

Children Victims of Terrorism Networks

#### Article 88

Special Protection for Children Victims of Terrorism Networks as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter k shall be carried out through efforts:  
a. education on education, ideology, and nationalism values;  
b. counseling on the dangers of terrorism;  
c. Social Rehabilitation; and  
d. Social Assistance.

#### Article 89

1. Education efforts on education as referred to in Article 91 letter a shall be carried out through:  
a. instilling moral and mental values in order to live in harmony and peace;  
b. teaching character education and good manners; and  
c. developing potential and personality as well as skills.  
2. Education on ideology for Children Victims of Terrorism Networks as referred to in Article 88 letter a shall be carried out by providing understanding on:  
a. Pancasila as the state ideology;  
b. history, meaning, function of Pancasila as the foundation of the state, philosophy, way of life, and unifier of the nation; and

3. Education on nationalism values as referred to in Article 88 letter a shall be carried out by providing understanding to:  
a. foster love for the nation and homeland;  
b. willingness to sacrifice for the nation and state;

Personality counseling as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out to understand the psychological condition of Children Victims of Terrorism Networks and encourage Children to be able to control themselves and express the interests and talents of Children in a positive manner.

f. connecting to institutions that handle Children Victims of Terrorism Networks; and

b. provision of required services including medicines that are inherent to Children with Disabilities.

b. involvement of Children with Disabilities in expressing views according to needs; and  
c. providing access for Children with Disabilities to develop themselves and utilize all abilities according to their talents and interests.

2. Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 108 dilakukan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.

### Paragraf 15

Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan Terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya

#### Pasal 113

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 32 ayat (1) huruf o dilakukan melalui Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial.

#### Pasal 114

Ketentuan mengenai Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 83 berlaku secara mutatis mutandis terhadap bentuk Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113.

#### Pasal 115

1. Anak yang telah mendapatkan Perlindungan Khusus sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113 dikembalikan -47- kepada keluarga atau Masyarakat.  
2. Sebelum dikembalikan kepada keluarga atau Masyarakat sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), langkah yang harus dilakukan:  
a. menyiapkan kondisi psikologis Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya untuk bersedia dikembalikan pada keluarga atau Masyarakat;  
b. memastikan keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat untuk menerima dan tidak lagi melakukan pelabelan dan diskriminasi terhadap Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya;  
c. menelusuri Keluarga Pengganti lain jika ada penolakan dari keluarga atau Masyarakat;  
d. memastikan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya dalam kondisi aman, nyaman, dan terpenuhi kebutuhannya; dan  
e. melakukan pemantauan dan evaluasi perkembangan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya yang telah dikembalikan kepada keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat.

#### Pasal 116

Langkah pemantauan dan evaluasi perkembangan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya yang telah dikembalikan kepada keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 115 ayat (2) huruf e dilaksanakan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten sesuai dengan tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangannya.

#### Pasal 117

Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113 dilakukan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten sesuai dengan tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangannya.

#### Pasal 118

Untuk mencegah terjadinya stigmatisasi dari pelabelan terhadap Anak terkait kondisi orang tuanya, Pemerintah Kabupaten melakukan:  
a. pemberian edukasi kepada Masyarakat serta berperan aktif untuk menghilangkan stigma terhadap Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi orang tuanya;  

b.pemberian ruang kepada Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi -48- orang tuanya untuk mendapatkan kegiatan rekreasional; dan
c. koordinasi dengan unit layanan yang menangani perlindungan Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi orang tuanya dalam hal terdapat potensi kekerasan dan diskriminasi terhadap Anak di Kabupaten.

## Bagian Keempat

Layanan atau Penanganan Rujukan Lanjutan bagi Anak Korban Kekerasan

#### Pasal 119

Dalam rangka perlindungan anak, Pemerintah Kabupaten berkewajiban:  
a. menyediakan layanan atau penanganan rujukan lanjutan; dan  
b. melakukan penguatan dan pengembangan lembaga penyedialayanan perlindungan perempuan dan anak.

#### Pasal 120

1. Penyediaan layanan atau penanganan rujukan lanjutan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 119 huruf a diperuntukkan bagi anak korban kekerasan yang memerlukan koordinasi tingkat Kabupaten.  
2. Penyediaaan layanan atau penanganan rujukan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan melalui unit PPA tingkat Kabupaten.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tugas, keanggaotaan, dan pembentukan unit PPA sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

# BAB IV

## PENINGKATAN KUALITAS KELUARGA

#### Pasal 121

Peningkatan kualitas keluarga dilaksanakan dalam rangka mewujudkan kesetaraan gender dan hak anak.

#### Pasal 122

Peningkatan kualitas keluarga dilakukan melalui:  
a. pencegahan perkawinan usia anak;  
b. pemenuhan hak anak atas ASI eksklusif;  
c. mendekatkan ibu pada pelayanan kesehatan;  
d. meningkatkan ketahanan keluarga.

#### Pasal 123

Pencegahan perkawinan usia anak sebagaimana dimaksud dalamPasal 122 huruf a bertujuan:  
a. meningkatkan produkstivitas anak perempuan;  
b. mengembangkan potensi diri anak perempuan;  
c. mencegah kehamilan di usia terlalu muda;  
d. menurunkan angka kematian ibu dan bayi;  
e. menurunkan angka kemiskinan; dan  
f. mencegah terjadinya kekerasan dalam rumah tangga.

Children Victims of Mistreatment and Neglect

Children With Deviant Social Behavior

The provisions regarding Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the form of Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 108.

Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling Related to the Condition of Their Parents
